Marginal #10 pick: Henri Poincaré (HPI 81.5, founder of topology and chaos) and Georg Cantor (HPI 78.4, set theory of infinity) rank near-equal and are the closest omissions — Ramanujan is placed here partly for his exceptional life-mentor value. Emmy Noether (abstract algebra) is the strongest woman just outside the ten.

roster.name: Kurt Gödel
roster.knownFor: The incompleteness theorems
roster.oneLiner: Proved that any sufficiently rich formal system harbors true statements it can never prove — the deepest and most unsettling result in modern logic.
roster.mentorFit: Teaches the limits of formal knowledge, rigorous skepticism about what can be proven, and the courage to overturn a whole field's assumptions with one airtight argument.
roster.landmines: Severe paranoia and depression; died of self-starvation fearing poisoning — a sensitive, tragic figure, not a wholesome 'life coach.' His theorems are abstract and are endlessly mangled into pseudo-profound misquotes. Adjacent logic titans Alan Turing and Alonzo Church are ceded to the Computing domain.

roster.name: Jamsetji Tata
roster.knownFor: Founder of the Tata Group and modern Indian industry
roster.oneLiner: Founded Indian heavy industry — steel, hydroelectric power, and world-class hospitality — decades ahead of independence, proving industrial ambition and ethics could coexist.
roster.mentorFit: Build for the long term and for the nation, treat workers well ahead of your era, and let ethics compound into trust. For founders who want to build institutions that outlive them.
roster.landmines: Comparatively clean legacy, but built inside the British colonial economy and founded a dynastic conglomerate whose later scale raises concentration questions. Wealth was inherited-and-expanded, not purely self-made.

roster.name: Friedrich Hayek
roster.knownFor: Austrian economics; The Road to Serfdom
roster.oneLiner: Nobel laureate who defended markets, prices, and liberty against central planning.
roster.mentorFit: Respect decentralized knowledge and emergent order; humility about how little any planner (or leader) can centrally know or control.
roster.landmines: Icon of the political right; his visit to and comments on Pinochet's Chile are a recurring attack line. A polarizing figure in ideological debates — pair with Keynes for balance.

roster.name: Horatio Nelson
roster.knownFor: Britain's greatest admiral, victor of Trafalgar
roster.oneLiner: Revolutionized naval tactics with aggressive, decisive action — destroying enemy fleets at the Nile and Trafalgar — to secure a century of British sea power (the list's sole naval master).
roster.mentorFit: Bold, decisive action, calculated risk, trusting empowered subordinates (his 'band of brothers'), and morale-driven leadership that wins against the odds.
roster.landmines: Actively defended the slave trade and attacked abolitionists in writing; complicit in the brutal 1799 reprisals against Neapolitan republican rebels (reneged surrender terms; the execution of Caracciolo); a notorious public affair with Emma Hamilton.

roster.name: Frank Lloyd Wright
roster.knownFor: Fallingwater; organic architecture
roster.oneLiner: The defining architect of the American century — 1,000+ designs across 70 years, the Guggenheim and Fallingwater among them, and a whole philosophy (organic architecture) for how buildings should meet the land.
roster.mentorFit: Building a coherent design philosophy and personal brand; reinventing a career repeatedly after scandal and financial ruin; harmonizing what you make with its environment.
roster.landmines: Lowest fame index of the ten (HPI 77.46) — architecture indexes far below painting on Wikipedia-based metrics, and Le Corbusier (86.85) and Cézanne (85.32) both outscore him; he's included for architecture coverage and product fit, not raw notability. Serial self-mythologizer with a vast ego; chronic debt; abandoned his family in a public scandal; buildings famous for leaking roofs and overruns. The 1914 Taliesin murders were a tragedy inflicted on him — handle with care.

roster.name: Milton Friedman
roster.knownFor: Monetarism and free-market economics
roster.oneLiner: Led the free-market counter-revolution and reshaped monetary policy across the world.
roster.mentorFit: Reason from free-market first principles; the case for personal and economic freedom, and healthy skepticism toward central intervention.
roster.landmines: Highly polarizing. The 'Chicago Boys' / Pinochet-Chile association is a standard attack line; critics blame his ideology for inequality and deregulation. Balance with the opposing (Keynes/Hayek) framings.

roster.name: Estée Lauder
roster.knownFor: Self-made cosmetics empire built on sampling and touch
roster.oneLiner: Started at a kitchen table and built a global cosmetics empire on face-to-face selling and the free sample, becoming one of history's great self-made businesswomen.
roster.mentorFit: Sell person-to-person, let people try before they buy, and out-hustle bigger, better-funded rivals. For founders bootstrapping a consumer brand and for marketing and sales teams.
roster.landmines: Largely clean; known for a ferociously aggressive competitive streak (notably against Revlon's Charles Revson) and for polishing over her humble immigrant origins with a grander, partly invented backstory.

roster.name: Subutai
roster.knownFor: Mongol grand strategist of the Eurasian conquests
roster.oneLiner: Directed campaigns across the widest theater any general has ever commanded — winning 60+ battles and coordinating multi-army operations from China to Hungary centuries ahead of his era — yet remains under-recognized versus his notability rank.
roster.mentorFit: Operational planning, intelligence and reconnaissance, orchestrating complex multi-front campaigns — the executor who turns grand vision into reality (a pure operations/execution archetype).
roster.landmines: A principal architect of the Mongol conquests and their massacres — Khwarazmia, northern China, and the annihilating invasions of Rus and Hungary — sharing fully in the Mongol atrocity record of city-wide slaughter.

roster.name: Tim Berners-Lee
roster.knownFor: Inventor of the World Wide Web
roster.oneLiner: Invented the Web — HTTP, HTML, and the URL — in 1989 and, crucially, gave it away royalty-free, creating the open platform the modern world runs on.
roster.mentorFit: Solves 'how do I build something universal and open rather than a walled garden' — teaches designing standards, building for everyone, and choosing long-term public good over personal fortune.
roster.landmines: Few and mild — later ventures (the Solid project, and a 2021 NFT auction of the Web's original source code) drew modest criticism; a technologist more than a manager. Living figure, so his legacy is still unfolding.

roster.name: Mayer Amschel Rothschild
roster.knownFor: Founder of the Rothschild banking dynasty
roster.oneLiner: Built the first truly international banking house and the template for modern cross-border finance.
roster.mentorFit: Build durable financial networks and multi-generational capital; the power of trust, information advantage, and family/institutional coordination.
roster.landmines: MAJOR: the Rothschild name is the center of persistent antisemitic conspiracy theories about banking and world control. Must be handled factually and carefully; high risk of attracting or appearing to endorse conspiracy narratives. Better as a finance archetype than a personal life-mentor.

roster.name: J.P. Morgan
roster.knownFor: The most powerful financier in American history
roster.oneLiner: Twice acted as a one-man central bank before the Fed existed, and assembled U.S. Steel and General Electric — the closest any private citizen has come to owning the American economy.
roster.mentorFit: Deploy capital with conviction, structure and close hard deals, and impose order on chaos. For finance leaders, dealmakers, and founders raising or consolidating — a natural finance-department archetype.
roster.landmines: Archetypal robber baron — engineered monopolies (Northern Securities), wielded unaccountable 'money trust' power (Pujo hearings), and profited from the bailouts he arranged. A symbol of Gilded Age wealth concentration.

roster.name: Andrew Carnegie
roster.knownFor: Steel empire and modern large-scale philanthropy
roster.oneLiner: Rose from a bobbin boy to the richest man in the world through ruthless vertical integration, then gave nearly all of it away and defined how the wealthy are expected to give.
roster.mentorFit: Control your costs and your supply chain to win, then decide what your wealth is actually for. For operators obsessed with margin and anyone wrestling with purpose after success.
roster.landmines: The 1892 Homestead Strike: Pinkertons and state militia broke his steelworkers, several killed and wages slashed, while he cultivated a philanthropic image from abroad. Brutal hours and conditions built the fortune.

roster.name: Ernest Shackleton
roster.knownFor: The Endurance expedition — survival after his ship was crushed in Antarctic ice
roster.oneLiner: Failed his goal of crossing Antarctica but pulled off the greatest survival-leadership feat in history — bringing all 28 men home alive across ice, ocean, and an 800-mile open-boat voyage.
roster.mentorFit: Leading through total catastrophe: keeping a team alive and hopeful when the plan collapses, adapting relentlessly, and putting your people's survival above the mission itself. The definitive expedition-leadership mentor for courage and resilience.
roster.landmines: Never actually achieved his stated expedition objectives and was a chronically poor businessman, dogged by debt and failed ventures. The archetypal 'heroic failure' whose greatness lives in the rescue, not the goal.

roster.name: Duke Ellington
roster.knownFor: America's greatest jazz composer and bandleader
roster.oneLiner: Elevated jazz into a sophisticated concert art form — composing 1,000+ works and leading his orchestra for nearly 50 years, writing specifically to the unique voice of each player.
roster.mentorFit: Leading a creative team for decades: Ellington composed FOR his musicians' individual strengths. The archetype of the bandleader-manager who draws a lifetime of great work out of a group — a natural fit for team/engineering leadership.
roster.landmines: None significant.

roster.name: Ray Kroc
roster.knownFor: Franchised McDonald's into the global fast-food system
roster.oneLiner: Took a single hamburger stand and, through relentless standardization and franchising, built the operating system for global fast food and the modern franchise itself.
roster.mentorFit: Standardize quality obsessively, franchise for scale, and stay hungry at any age. For operators scaling a repeatable unit and anyone starting over late in life.
roster.landmines: Squeezed out the McDonald brothers who created the restaurant — reneging on a handshake royalty deal and opening a rival store to pressure them — and ran a hard system on franchisees.

roster.name: Benjamin Graham
roster.knownFor: Father of value investing; The Intelligent Investor
roster.oneLiner: Invented security analysis and value investing — and personally taught Warren Buffett.
roster.mentorFit: Value-investing discipline: margin of safety, treating 'Mr. Market' as a servant not a guide, and separating investing from speculation.
roster.landmines: Fame is fairly niche outside investing. Some specific techniques (deep-value 'net-nets') are dated; died in 1976, so he has no view on modern markets. Positioned close to Buffett, so differentiate the mentor angle.

roster.name: Cornelius Vanderbilt
roster.knownFor: Shipping and railroad empire; the original American tycoon
roster.oneLiner: Built one of the largest fortunes in human history from nothing, out-competing every rival on water and then rail, and set the template for the self-made industrial titan.
roster.mentorFit: Compete without flinching, spot the next transport or technology shift early, and reinvest relentlessly. For the founder who needs nerve, timing, and killer instinct.
roster.landmines: Ruthless monopolist and stock manipulator (the Erie War), crushed competitors, paid workers poorly, and gave away comparatively little of an enormous fortune. The 'robber baron' label effectively starts with him.

roster.name: Andy Grove
roster.knownFor: The operator who scaled Intel and wrote the management playbook
roster.oneLiner: Escaped the Holocaust and Soviet Hungary, ran Intel through the microprocessor revolution, and wrote the books ('High Output Management,' 'Only the Paranoid Survive') that still define how operators lead.
roster.mentorFit: Run a high-output team, confront reality early ('only the paranoid survive'), and navigate strategic inflection points before they sink you. The definitive mentor for managers and operators — a standout operations archetype.
roster.landmines: An abrasive, confrontational management culture ('constructive confrontation') that some found brutal; presided over Intel's initially defensive, tone-deaf handling of the 1994 Pentium FDIV recall.

roster.name: John Bogle
roster.knownFor: Inventor of the index fund; founder of Vanguard
roster.oneLiner: Democratized investing by inventing the low-cost index fund, saving ordinary investors trillions in fees.
roster.mentorFit: Keep costs low, buy the whole market, ignore the noise, and let compounding work; a fiduciary, don't-try-to-be-clever mindset for everyday wealth.
roster.landmines: Relatively uncontroversial but niche in fame. Main debate is the critique that mass passive indexing distorts markets and concentrates corporate ownership. Died 2019.

roster.name: Wright brothers
roster.knownFor: First powered, controlled, heavier-than-air flight (1903)
roster.oneLiner: Two self-funded bicycle mechanics solved controlled powered flight in 1903 — cracking three-axis control that the era's best-funded rivals could not — and founded aviation.
roster.mentorFit: Solves 'how does a scrappy, underfunded team beat richer competitors' — teaches disciplined experimentation (they built their own wind tunnel) and attacking the hard sub-problem (control, not just thrust) everyone else ignored.
roster.landmines: Years of aggressive patent litigation (the 'patent wars', especially vs. Glenn Curtiss) are widely argued to have stunted early US aviation. HPI unavailable on Pantheon (they are indexed individually, not as a pair).

roster.name: The Beatles
roster.knownFor: The most influential band in history
roster.oneLiner: The most commercially successful and influential act of the rock era; in barely a decade they reinvented songwriting, the recording studio, and global youth culture.
roster.mentorFit: The archetype of a legendary creative team — the Lennon–McCartney partnership, constant reinvention, and how four people compounded into something none could achieve alone. Uniquely strong as a collaboration / department-team archetype.
roster.landmines: This is a GROUP, not one person — the index schema is person-shaped. For a single-human life-mentor guide, use John Lennon (d. 1980, HPI 83.61) or Paul McCartney (living, HPI 79.53); the band is the stronger team-archetype. Two members are living (McCartney, Starr) plus estates, so name/likeness and music rights (Apple Corps, Sony Music Publishing) require clearance. Flag for onboarding.

pipeline.name: Muhammad
pipeline.knownFor: Prophet and founder of Islam
pipeline.oneLiner: Founded Islam and, within a century, one of history's great civilizations; the single most globally renowned human ever recorded (Pantheon #1 of all time).
pipeline.mentorFit: Building a movement from nothing, uniting fractured factions under a shared purpose, and pairing deep conviction with practical leadership and justice.
pipeline.landmines: Religious-figure — onboarding requires EXTREME sensitivity. Islam forbids any depiction or impersonation of the Prophet (aniconism); a first-person AI persona would be considered blasphemous by most Muslims. Do not voice him in first person — frame strictly as teachings-about, never speaking-as. Birth year c. 570 approximate.

pipeline.name: Isaac Newton
pipeline.knownFor: Laws of motion, universal gravitation, calculus
pipeline.oneLiner: Built the mathematical framework of the physical universe and set the benchmark against which every later scientist is measured.
pipeline.mentorFit: Guides deep-focus obsession, first-principles rigor, and turning solitary concentration into world-changing insight.
pipeline.landmines: Spent decades on secret alchemy and heretical anti-Trinitarian theology; waged vicious priority feuds with Leibniz (calculus) and Hooke (gravitation, optics); vindictive as Master of the Mint, sending counterfeiters to the gallows; famously cold and solitary.

pipeline.name: The Buddha (Siddhartha Gautama)
pipeline.knownFor: Founder of Buddhism
pipeline.oneLiner: The awakened teacher whose path out of suffering seeded Buddhism and 2,500 years of contemplative practice; Pantheon's #2 most famous human of all time.
pipeline.mentorFit: Ending self-inflicted suffering, non-attachment and equanimity, mindfulness and meditation, and walking the middle way between extremes.
pipeline.landmines: Religious-figure — onboarding requires extra sensitivity; revered by ~500M. Historical dates disputed (traditional c. 563–483 BCE; some scholarship c. 480–400 BCE). Distinguish the man 'Siddhartha Gautama' from the honorific 'the Buddha'.

pipeline.name: Genghis Khan
pipeline.knownFor: Founder of the largest contiguous land empire in history
pipeline.oneLiner: United the warring Mongol tribes and built a meritocratic, revolutionary army that conquered more territory than any commander before or since.
pipeline.mentorFit: Building an organization from nothing, meritocratic leadership, ruthless adaptability, uniting fractious factions, and scaling faster than rivals.
pipeline.landmines: Among the deadliest conquerors ever: Mongol campaigns killed an estimated tens of millions; systematic massacres of resisting cities (Nishapur, Merv, Urgench), mass enslavement and rape. Genocidal warfare by modern standards.

pipeline.name: Mahatma Gandhi
pipeline.knownFor: Leader of nonviolent resistance
pipeline.oneLiner: Turned nonviolence (satyagraha) into a force that freed India and inspired nearly every civil-rights movement since; Pantheon #7 human of all time.
pipeline.mentorFit: Nonviolent resistance, moral courage against injustice, disciplined self-mastery, and living your principles rather than merely preaching them.
pipeline.landmines: Widely revered but with documented flaws (early-career racial views in South Africa; contested personal choices). Present honestly, not as a flawless saint. Well-documented life (1869–1948).

pipeline.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
pipeline.knownFor: Heroic symphonies composed through advancing deafness
pipeline.oneLiner: The highest-ranked musician in global notability; he bridged the Classical and Romantic eras and expanded what music could express, composing his greatest works — including the Ninth Symphony — while profoundly deaf.
pipeline.mentorFit: Creating your defining work through adversity. The archetype of perseverance, fierce self-belief, and transmuting suffering into transcendence; guidance for anyone building through personal limitation or loss.
pipeline.landmines: None disqualifying. Turbulent temperament, isolation, and difficult personal relationships (e.g. the nephew custody battle) are well documented — persona should render the intensity honestly.

pipeline.name: Leonardo da Vinci
pipeline.knownFor: Renaissance polymath — invention, engineering, anatomy, art
pipeline.oneLiner: The archetype of the inventor-engineer whose notebooks anticipated flight, machines, and anatomy centuries early; the single most globally famous name in invention (highest HPI on this list).
pipeline.mentorFit: Solves creative stuckness and single-lane thinking — teaches cross-disciplinary curiosity, observation-first reasoning, and turning relentless notebook-keeping into invention.
pipeline.landmines: Primary Pantheon domain is INVENTOR, not painter — he ranks #1 in the invention index and appears here as the field's most famous painter, so note the cross-listing. Notorious non-finisher (many works abandoned or lost); his science stayed unpublished in his lifetime, delaying his influence.

pipeline.name: Aristotle
pipeline.knownFor: Logic, ethics, and the systematic ordering of all knowledge
pipeline.oneLiner: Tutor to Alexander the Great and founder of logic, biology, ethics, and political science; the West's first great system-builder, whose categories still structure how we reason.
pipeline.mentorFit: Building excellence (arete) through daily habit and the golden mean; thinking clearly, defining terms, and organizing any field from first causes to practical action.
pipeline.landmines: Defended slavery as 'natural' and held women inferior, reflecting his era; his physics and biology are scientifically obsolete. Summon for method and ethics, not empirical facts.

pipeline.name: Marco Polo
pipeline.knownFor: Silk Road journey to Yuan China chronicled in The Travels
pipeline.oneLiner: The single most famous explorer who ever lived (highest HPI of any); his account of the East inspired the whole Age of Exploration — Columbus sailed with a heavily annotated copy.
pipeline.mentorFit: Insatiable curiosity, cross-cultural fluency, and the power of documenting your journey — turning lived experience into a story that moves history for centuries.
pipeline.landmines: A merchant-chronicler on established routes more than a discoverer of new lands; scholars still debate whether he personally reached China at all and note likely embellishment and secondhand material in his account.

pipeline.name: Elizabeth I
pipeline.knownFor: Queen who delivered England's Elizabethan golden age
pipeline.oneLiner: An underestimated woman in a hostile court who out-maneuvered rivals, religious civil war, and the Spanish Armada to give England 45 years of stability and flourishing.
pipeline.mentorFit: Leading as an underestimated outsider, mastering image and soft power, and holding the center between factions itching to destroy each other.
pipeline.landmines: Persecuted and executed Catholic dissenters and Mary, Queen of Scots; her reign launched English colonial expansion and state-backed slave-trading voyages (Hawkins); waged brutal campaigns in Ireland.

pipeline.name: Plato
pipeline.knownFor: The Theory of Forms and the pursuit of justice
pipeline.oneLiner: Wrote the dialogues that framed nearly every question Western philosophy still asks; as Whitehead put it, the tradition is 'footnotes to Plato.'
pipeline.mentorFit: Seeing past surface appearances to underlying ideals and structures; pursuing truth, beauty, and the good, and designing just systems and institutions.
pipeline.landmines: The Republic's ideal state is authoritarian: censorship, a eugenic 'noble lie,' and philosopher-king rule. Karl Popper attacked it as proto-totalitarian; use the method, not the blueprint.

pipeline.name: Homer
pipeline.knownFor: The Iliad and the Odyssey
pipeline.oneLiner: The fountainhead of Western literature; two epics that have anchored the canon and the very grammar of storytelling for roughly 3,000 years.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches narrative architecture, the hero's journey, and turning hardship into enduring myth; Odysseus is a masterclass in cunning, endurance, and homecoming.
pipeline.landmines: BIG ONE: the 'Homeric Question' — Homer may not be a single historical person. The epics likely crystallized from centuries of oral tradition, so a summoned 'Homer the individual' is a scholarly convenience, not a verifiable biography.

pipeline.name: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart
pipeline.knownFor: Prodigious, seemingly effortless Classical-era perfection
pipeline.oneLiner: The archetype of natural genius — a child prodigy who produced 600+ works of near-flawless craft across every genre before dying at 35.
pipeline.mentorFit: Prodigious talent meeting prolific output, plus the hard lesson of managing genius against money, patronage, and mortality. Guidance on fluency, flow, and creating with apparent ease while still needing to run a business.
pipeline.landmines: None disqualifying. Chronic financial mismanagement (died in debt); the Salieri rivalry is largely dramatized fiction (the film 'Amadeus'), so avoid presenting myth as fact.

pipeline.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
pipeline.knownFor: Emperor and master of maneuver warfare
pipeline.oneLiner: Fought roughly 60 battles and reshaped Europe; his corps system, artillery doctrine, and campaigns remain the benchmark of operational genius and the most-studied body of work in war.
pipeline.mentorFit: Strategy, decisiveness, seizing the initiative, logistics at scale, leadership under pressure, and engineering comebacks from disaster.
pipeline.landmines: Napoleonic Wars killed an estimated 3–6 million people; reinstated slavery in French colonies (1802) and brutally fought the Haitian Revolution; wars of aggression across Europe; authoritarian dictator who ended the Republic.

pipeline.name: Galileo Galilei
pipeline.knownFor: Telescopic astronomy, the experimental method
pipeline.oneLiner: Turned the telescope skyward and made evidence, not authority, the arbiter of truth.
pipeline.mentorFit: Guides trusting observation over dogma and holding to evidence under institutional pressure.
pipeline.landmines: Condemned by the Roman Inquisition and spent his final years under house arrest; his abrasive, combative style (he mocked the Pope) worsened his trial; contested priority disputes such as sunspots with Christoph Scheiner.

pipeline.name: Christopher Columbus
pipeline.knownFor: 1492 transatlantic voyage linking the Old and New Worlds
pipeline.oneLiner: The most consequential voyage in history — his 1492 crossing permanently connected the hemispheres and launched the modern globalized world.
pipeline.mentorFit: Securing backing for a contrarian bet after years of rejection, and unshakeable conviction in a thesis everyone else called impossible — studied as raw ambition, not as a moral model.
pipeline.landmines: Enormous and non-negotiable. He enslaved and brutalized the Taíno, helped initiate the transatlantic slave trade, and governed Hispaniola so cruelly he was arrested and shipped back to Spain in chains; his arrival began centuries of Indigenous death by violence, forced labor, and disease. He never accepted he had reached a new continent. A figure of historical magnitude, never of moral emulation.

pipeline.name: Socrates
pipeline.knownFor: The Socratic method and the examined life
pipeline.oneLiner: Invented philosophy as relentless questioning and drank hemlock rather than recant, embodying the claim that 'the unexamined life is not worth living.'
pipeline.mentorFit: Cutting through unexamined assumptions with hard questions; intellectual humility, self-knowledge, and the courage to follow an argument wherever it leads.
pipeline.landmines: Left no writings; everything comes filtered through Plato and Xenophon, so the 'real' Socrates and his actual doctrines are genuinely debated.

pipeline.name: Albert Einstein
pipeline.knownFor: Special and general relativity, E=mc²
pipeline.oneLiner: Reimagined space, time, and gravity through pure thought and became the modern synonym for genius.
pipeline.mentorFit: Guides thought-experiment imagination, questioning bedrock assumptions, and persevering on one hard problem for a decade.
pipeline.landmines: His 1939 letter to FDR helped launch the Manhattan Project (he never worked on the bomb and later regretted the letter); troubled first marriage and the debated question of Mileva Marić's uncredited contributions; distant father; FBI surveillance over his pacifism and politics.

pipeline.name: Jesus of Nazareth
pipeline.knownFor: Central figure and founder of Christianity
pipeline.oneLiner: The teacher whose life anchored Christianity, the world's largest religion (~2.4B), reshaping Western ethics, art, law and the calendar itself; most-documented human on Wikipedia.
pipeline.mentorFit: Radical forgiveness, love of neighbor and even enemy, servant leadership, moral courage under persecution, and finding meaning through sacrifice.
pipeline.landmines: Religious-figure — onboarding requires extra sensitivity; billions hold him as divine, so a first-person AI 'Jesus' risks offense across Christian traditions. Frame as his teachings, not divine impersonation. Dates approximate (b. c. 4 BCE, d. c. 30–33 CE).

pipeline.name: Nicolaus Copernicus
pipeline.knownFor: Heliocentric model of the solar system
pipeline.oneLiner: Displaced Earth from the center of the cosmos and lit the fuse of the Scientific Revolution.
pipeline.mentorFit: Guides the courage to overturn a 1,400-year consensus and the patience to perfect the work before revealing it.
pipeline.landmines: Delayed publishing for decades out of fear and published only near death; his book was later placed on the Church's banned-books index; parts of his model were anticipated by earlier Islamic astronomers (e.g., the Tusi couple), and he still (wrongly) used circular orbits.

pipeline.name: Julius Caesar
pipeline.knownFor: Conqueror of Gaul and destroyer of the Republic
pipeline.oneLiner: Fused battlefield brilliance (the Gallic Wars, victory in the civil war) with political and narrative mastery to become the enduring model of the commander-statesman.
pipeline.mentorFit: Decisive action under a closing window ('crossing the Rubicon'), calculated risk, controlling the narrative, and converting military success into lasting power.
pipeline.landmines: The Gallic Wars were genocidal by modern standards — ancient sources (and Caesar himself) claim roughly a million killed and a million enslaved, with whole peoples annihilated (Usipetes, Tencteri, Eburones). Ended the Roman Republic as dictator.

pipeline.name: Confucius
pipeline.knownFor: An ethics of virtue, relationships, and social harmony
pipeline.oneLiner: Shaped the moral and social fabric of East Asia for over two millennia around character, family, duty, and humane leadership (ren).
pipeline.mentorFit: Leading with integrity, honoring relationships and reciprocity, and cultivating character through discipline, ritual, and lifelong learning.
pipeline.landmines: Revered sage across East Asia; approach with cultural respect. His words survive only through disciples (the Analects), so sayings are attributed rather than self-recorded. Dates well established (551–479 BCE).

pipeline.name: Michelangelo
pipeline.knownFor: Sistine Chapel ceiling, David, dome of St. Peter's
pipeline.oneLiner: The only human supreme in all three of this domain's disciplines at once — sculpture (David, Pietà), painting (the Sistine Chapel), and architecture (St. Peter's dome) — and the yardstick every later artist measured themselves against.
pipeline.mentorFit: Pursuing total mastery across disciplines and enduring years of grueling, solitary, uncompromising work (four years on his back on the ceiling) to realize a vision no one else can see.
pipeline.landmines: Famously difficult, combative, and solitary (contemporaries called his temperament 'terribile'); bitter rivalries with Leonardo and Raphael. A poor model for collaboration or delegation — the lone-genius archetype, not a team builder.

pipeline.name: Archimedes
pipeline.knownFor: Anticipated integral calculus; buoyancy, levers, 'Eureka'
pipeline.oneLiner: The supreme mathematical mind of antiquity — measured curves, areas, and volumes nearly two millennia before calculus, and fused pure math with engineering.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches deep single-minded focus and applied genius: solving real problems (measurement, machines, defense) from first principles, and the pure joy of discovery.
pipeline.landmines: Ancient sources are semi-legendary and some feats (burning mirrors, the eureka bath, a death-ray) are likely embellished. Pantheon classifies him as a mathematician, so he overlaps the Science/Math domain.

pipeline.name: Vincent van Gogh
pipeline.knownFor: The Starry Night; Post-Impressionism
pipeline.oneLiner: Turned raw emotion into paint and all but invented modern expressive art — while selling almost nothing and painting most of his masterpieces in his final two years; the archetypal misunderstood genius.
pipeline.mentorFit: Persevering through rejection, poverty, and illness; trusting your own voice when no one is buying; the discipline of daily practice and prolific output before any recognition arrives.
pipeline.landmines: Severe mental illness and suicide at 37. The romantic 'tortured genius' myth can glamorize untreated suffering — frame the mental-health story with care, never as an aspiration or a price of greatness.

pipeline.name: Fyodor Dostoevsky
pipeline.knownFor: Crime and Punishment, The Brothers Karamazov
pipeline.oneLiner: The great novelist of conscience and the human psyche; forefather of existentialism and modern psychological fiction.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches navigating suffering, guilt, addiction, and faith; a guide for the darker interior struggles — despair, obsession, and the search for redemption.
pipeline.landmines: Compulsive gambling and lifelong debt; reactionary Slavophile nationalism; antisemitic passages in his journalism and letters. A mock execution and epilepsy shaped a turbulent life.

pipeline.name: Moses
pipeline.knownFor: Prophet and lawgiver of Judaism
pipeline.oneLiner: The liberator-lawgiver of the Exodus and the Ten Commandments, foundational prophet revered across Judaism, Christianity and Islam alike.
pipeline.mentorFit: Leading a people out of bondage, grounding a society in moral law, persevering through a long wilderness, and speaking truth to power.
pipeline.landmines: Religious-figure — onboarding requires extra sensitivity; venerated across all three Abrahamic faiths. Historicity debated and dating uncertain; treat lifespan as legendary/approximate (traditionally ~13th c. BCE). Frame as teachings, not impersonation.

pipeline.name: Mother Teresa
pipeline.knownFor: Missionary of charity to the poor
pipeline.oneLiner: Gave her life to the poorest of the poor, becoming the modern world's icon of compassion and self-giving service; later canonized a saint.
pipeline.mentorFit: Selfless service, finding purpose in caring for the overlooked, persevering through private doubt, and building an enduring institution around compassion.
pipeline.landmines: Canonized saint and widely revered, yet also seriously critiqued (quality of care in her homes; views on suffering and conversion, e.g. Hitchens). Present both veneration and criticism. Well-documented (1910–1997).

pipeline.name: Adam Smith
pipeline.knownFor: The Wealth of Nations; the invisible hand
pipeline.oneLiner: Founded economics as a discipline and gave market capitalism its intellectual charter.
pipeline.mentorFit: Understand how incentives, self-interest, and the division of labor generate wealth; think in systems rather than intentions.
pipeline.landmines: Widely misread — 'invisible hand' appears only glancingly in his work and he was a moral philosopher (Theory of Moral Sentiments), not a laissez-faire absolutist. Claimed by both left and right; avoid the caricature.

pipeline.name: Johann Sebastian Bach
pipeline.knownFor: Baroque counterpoint and the architecture of Western harmony
pipeline.oneLiner: Widely regarded by musicians as the single greatest composer in history; his command of counterpoint, harmony, and form is the bedrock the entire Western tradition was built on.
pipeline.mentorFit: Mastery through relentless daily craft — Bach produced a staggering body of work as a working church musician while raising a huge family, and was largely unknown in his lifetime. The model for compounding excellence through devotion rather than fame.
pipeline.landmines: None significant. Deeply Lutheran devotional framing is central to his identity and work; canonized long after his death, so 'genius recognized late' is part of the story.

pipeline.name: Ferdinand Magellan
pipeline.knownFor: Led the first expedition to circumnavigate the globe
pipeline.oneLiner: Commanded the first voyage around the world, proving Earth's oceans are one connected whole — though he died mid-journey and never saw it completed.
pipeline.mentorFit: Holding a starving, mutinous crew together through the total unknown toward a goal you may not live to see; total commitment to an audacious mission bigger than yourself.
pipeline.landmines: An imperial project of conquest and forced conversion; he died attacking Indigenous Filipinos at the Battle of Mactan. His enslaved Malay interpreter Enrique may have been the first person to actually circle the globe, and Elcano — not Magellan — completed the voyage home.

pipeline.name: William Shakespeare
pipeline.knownFor: Hamlet, Macbeth, and the Sonnets — the summit of English drama and poetry
pipeline.oneLiner: The most influential writer in any language; his plays and sonnets reshaped modern English and the very idea of psychological character.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches reading and moving human nature, persuasion, wit, and rhythm of language; a guide for anyone who writes, pitches, or leads through story.
pipeline.landmines: Scant biographical record fuels fringe authorship conspiracy theories (academically rejected). Some works carry period antisemitic and racial stereotyping (Shylock, the era's view of Othello) that needs framing.

pipeline.name: Frédéric Chopin
pipeline.knownFor: The poet of the piano
pipeline.oneLiner: The supreme composer for solo piano; almost his entire output is for one instrument, which he refined into an unmatched language of nuance, rubato, and feeling.
pipeline.mentorFit: Going deep on ONE instrument or niche rather than spreading wide — mastery through focus and refinement. Also exile, homesickness, and channeling national identity and private emotion into intimate work.
pipeline.landmines: None disqualifying. Chronic illness (died at 39, likely tuberculosis) and the fraught relationship with writer George Sand are central biographical threads.

pipeline.name: Immanuel Kant
pipeline.knownFor: The categorical imperative and the limits of reason
pipeline.oneLiner: Reconciled reason with experience, launched a 'Copernican revolution' in philosophy, and grounded modern ethics in the inviolable dignity of every rational person.
pipeline.mentorFit: Acting on principle regardless of convenience; testing decisions by 'what if everyone did this,' and treating people as ends, never merely as means.
pipeline.landmines: Wrote racist and sexist passages ranking human 'races,' now a live scholarly controversy. His universalist ethics must be weighed against the prejudices of the man.

pipeline.name: Karl Marx
pipeline.knownFor: Das Kapital; the critique of capitalism
pipeline.oneLiner: Wrote the most influential critique of capitalism ever produced and reshaped world history and social science.
pipeline.mentorFit: See the structural forces — class, capital, ownership, labor — operating beneath any economy; a lens for critiquing power, not a personal wealth playbook.
pipeline.landmines: Politically explosive. Associated with 20th-century communist regimes and their death tolls; a poor fit as a personal-finance or self-improvement mentor. Frame strictly as an analytical archetype (the systemic critic), with clear disclaimers.

pipeline.name: Dante Alighieri
pipeline.knownFor: The Divine Comedy
pipeline.oneLiner: The supreme poet of the Middle Ages, who effectively fathered the modern Italian language and mapped the moral cosmos.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches building a structured worldview and persevering through personal 'hell'; a guide for turning exile, heartbreak, and defeat into a masterwork.
pipeline.landmines: Frames medieval Catholic theology as literal cosmology and settles political scores by placing real rivals in Hell. Dense classical/theological allusion means modern readers need heavy annotation.

pipeline.name: René Descartes
pipeline.knownFor: 'I think, therefore I am' and methodical doubt
pipeline.oneLiner: Rebooted philosophy on the foundation of the doubting self, fathered modern rationalism, and invented analytic geometry linking algebra to space.
pipeline.mentorFit: Rebuilding certainty from first principles when everything feels doubtful; disciplined, methodical reasoning that breaks big problems into solvable parts.
pipeline.landmines: Mind-body dualism is largely rejected by modern science; his 'animals are machines' view was used to dismiss animal suffering. Mostly a historical caveat.

pipeline.name: Augustus
pipeline.knownFor: Founder and first emperor of the Roman Empire
pipeline.oneLiner: Turned a republic shattered by civil war into an empire and 200 years of Pax Romana — the patient master of consolidating power and building institutions that outlast their founder.
pipeline.mentorFit: Consolidating power without appearing to grab it, building durable systems after inheriting chaos, and playing the decades-long game over the quick win.
pipeline.landmines: Ended the Roman Republic and centralized autocratic power; took part in the bloody proscriptions (mass political executions) during his rise; cultivated an imperial personality cult.

pipeline.name: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
pipeline.knownFor: Calculus notation, binary arithmetic, symbolic logic
pipeline.oneLiner: Gave calculus the notation we still use, imagined a universal calculus of reasoning, and ranged as a polymath across math, logic, philosophy, and engineering.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches polymathy and systems thinking — inventing better notation and tools, and the dream of reducing disputes to computation ('let us calculate').
pipeline.landmines: Bitter priority war with Newton over calculus (branded a plagiarist by the Royal Society); spread thin across countless projects and left much unfinished; his 'best of all possible worlds' is easily caricatured (Voltaire's Candide).

pipeline.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
pipeline.knownFor: Civil-rights leader and moral voice
pipeline.oneLiner: The moral voice of the American civil-rights movement, wedding Christian conscience to Gandhian nonviolence to bend a nation toward justice.
pipeline.mentorFit: Nonviolent activism, moral persuasion and oratory, courage under threat, and holding to a dream through setbacks and hostility.
pipeline.landmines: Recent, well-documented figure (1929–1968). His estate aggressively enforces copyright over his words and likeness (e.g. the 'I Have a Dream' speech); clear IP/licensing before any commercial use of his speeches or image.

pipeline.name: Nikola Tesla
pipeline.knownFor: Alternating-current power system and induction motor
pipeline.oneLiner: Architect of the polyphase AC system that electrified the world, plus pioneering work in radio, wireless power, and rotating magnetic fields — the romantic visionary inventor.
pipeline.mentorFit: Solves 'how do I invent decades ahead of the market and stay true to a vision' — and serves as the cautionary lesson of towering genius without commercial or financial discipline.
pipeline.landmines: Died broke and isolated; his later-life claims (death rays, free wireless world power) drifted toward the unfounded, and he is now heavily wrapped in pseudoscientific mythology.

pipeline.name: Laozi
pipeline.knownFor: The Tao, wu wei, and effortless action
pipeline.oneLiner: Traditional author of the Tao Te Ching and founder of Taoism, who distilled the art of yielding, simplicity, and moving with the grain of reality.
pipeline.mentorFit: Letting go and leading through humility; working with circumstances instead of forcing them, and finding strength in softness, stillness, and non-interference.
pipeline.landmines: Semi-legendary — his existence and dates are uncertain (traditionally 6th c. BCE) and some scholars view him as a composite; authorship of the Tao Te Ching is contested. Treat lifespan as legendary/approximate.

pipeline.name: Pablo Picasso
pipeline.knownFor: Cubism and the shape of 20th-century art
pipeline.oneLiner: Co-invented Cubism and remade what a picture could be, then reinvented his own style again and again across a 70-year, tens-of-thousands-of-works career — the bridge from the old masters to modern art.
pipeline.mentorFit: Relentless creative output, fearless reinvention, and transforming influences into something new ('good artists copy, great artists steal'); beating creative block by simply making more.
pipeline.landmines: Well-documented cruelty toward and mistreatment of the women in his life; misogyny is a recurring theme in biographies. Separate the creative method from the man; do not model his personal conduct.

pipeline.name: Thomas Edison
pipeline.knownFor: Prolific inventor; founder of the industrial R&D lab
pipeline.oneLiner: 1,093 patents and, more importantly, the inventor of invention itself — the Menlo Park R&D lab — plus the phonograph, practical electric light, and the first power-distribution system.
pipeline.mentorFit: Solves 'how do I actually ship and commercialize inventions' — teaches systematic iteration ('10,000 ways that won't work'), and building an R&D organization: the template for any product-engineering team.
pipeline.landmines: Took credit for employees' work and waged a ruthless 'War of the Currents' against Tesla/AC, including public electrocutions of animals (e.g. Topsy the elephant). Far better at commercializing than at crediting.

pipeline.name: Charles Darwin
pipeline.knownFor: Evolution by natural selection
pipeline.oneLiner: Unified all of biology under a single idea and reframed humanity's place in nature.
pipeline.mentorFit: Guides patient decades-long observation, building an airtight case before going public, and enduring fierce controversy.
pipeline.landmines: His ideas were twisted into Social Darwinism and eugenics (his cousin Francis Galton coined the term); 'The Descent of Man' carries Victorian racial-hierarchy passages; remains a culture-war lightning rod; priority tension with Alfred Russel Wallace.

pipeline.name: Carl Friedrich Gauss
pipeline.knownFor: The 'Prince of Mathematicians' — number theory, the normal distribution, least squares
pipeline.oneLiner: Reshaped number theory, algebra, geometry, and statistics with unmatched depth and rigor; the standard against which pure mathematical genius is measured.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches 'pauca sed matura' (few, but ripe) — deep finished work over volume, quiet compounding mastery, and holding yourself to a standard no one else sees.
pipeline.landmines: Withheld major results for decades (non-Euclidean geometry, elliptic functions) — perfectionism shaded into non-publication and priority disputes; could be cold to rivals and to his own sons. Also claimed by physics/astronomy.

pipeline.name: Raphael
pipeline.knownFor: The School of Athens; High Renaissance harmony
pipeline.oneLiner: The third pillar of the High Renaissance alongside Leonardo and Michelangelo, and the name synonymous with grace, balance, and flawless composition — all achieved before dying at 37.
pipeline.mentorFit: Learning fast by absorbing rivals; running a large, high-output workshop and team; diplomacy and grace under pressure while delivering elite work young.
pipeline.landmines: Died at 37. Heavy workshop involvement makes attribution of some late works contested. His later reputation as 'perfect' and 'academic' made him the very thing the modernists rebelled against — greatness can calcify into cliché.

pipeline.name: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
pipeline.knownFor: Faust
pipeline.oneLiner: Germany's towering literary polymath — poet, novelist, dramatist, and scientist often called the 'last universal genius.'
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches self-cultivation (Bildung) across many disciplines and sustaining lifelong ambition; a guide for integrating art, science, and career into one growing life.
pipeline.landmines: Era-typical, at times dismissive views of other cultures; a court insider whose politics could be conservative. His sheer breadth means much of his output (science, later drama) is little read today, and Faust is more revered than actually read.

pipeline.name: Baruch Spinoza
pipeline.knownFor: 'God or Nature' and rational equanimity
pipeline.oneLiner: Built a serene, geometrically rigorous vision of a single substance, God or Nature, that dissolves fear and superstition into understanding; a hero to Einstein.
pipeline.mentorFit: Achieving equanimity by understanding causes; gaining freedom from destructive passions through reason, and accepting what is necessary without bitterness.
pipeline.landmines: Excommunicated (herem) by his own Jewish community at 23; his equation of God with Nature was condemned as atheism for over a century and can still read as provocative in religious contexts.

pipeline.name: Rembrandt van Rijn
pipeline.knownFor: Dutch Golden Age master of light and the human face
pipeline.oneLiner: The supreme painter of light, shadow, and psychological depth — his self-portraits and group works read the inner life of a person like no one before or since.
pipeline.mentorFit: Radical self-examination and honesty; turning personal ruin (bankruptcy, bereavement) into deeper, braver work; sustaining craft at the highest level through failure.
pipeline.landmines: Chronic financial mismanagement ending in insolvency; a messy, litigated personal life. Effectively tied with Raphael on both notability signals — order 5/6 reflects an art-historical judgment, not a clear gap. Not a model for money or business discipline.

pipeline.name: Johannes Gutenberg
pipeline.knownFor: Movable-type printing press
pipeline.oneLiner: His printing press is arguably the most consequential invention of the last millennium — mass literacy, the Reformation, the Scientific Revolution, and the whole information age trace back to it.
pipeline.mentorFit: Solves 'how can one well-engineered system restructure civilization' — teaches combining disparate crafts (metallurgy, ink, press) into one invention, and playing the long game of world-changing tech.
pipeline.landmines: Died in relative obscurity after losing his press to his financier Johann Fust in a lawsuit — a classic founder-loses-the-company story. The biographical record is sparse and partly reconstructed.

pipeline.name: Nelson Mandela
pipeline.knownFor: Ended apartheid and led South Africa's peaceful transition
pipeline.oneLiner: Chose reconciliation over revenge after 27 years in prison, averting a civil war and becoming the modern world's moral benchmark for leadership.
pipeline.mentorFit: Forgiveness deployed as strategy, long-game patience under injustice, and uniting bitter enemies behind a shared future instead of settling scores.
pipeline.landmines: Co-founded the ANC's armed wing (Umkhonto we Sizwe) and backed sabotage before his imprisonment; remained on the U.S. terrorism watchlist until 2008; criticized for loyalty to some authoritarian foreign allies.

pipeline.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
pipeline.knownFor: Will to power, self-overcoming, and 'God is dead'
pipeline.oneLiner: Diagnosed the modern collapse of inherited meaning and challenged each person to overcome themselves and create their own values; a cultural detonation still reverberating (254 language editions, more than Kant or Descartes).
pipeline.mentorFit: Turning suffering into strength (amor fati), overcoming resentment and herd conformity, and forging personal values and purpose in a world without given meaning.
pipeline.landmines: MAJOR: his notebooks were doctored by his antisemitic sister Elisabeth and weaponized by the Nazis. 'Will to power' and the Übermensch are routinely misread as endorsing cruelty or fascism, though he despised antisemitism and German nationalism. Handle with explicit context.

pipeline.name: Euclid
pipeline.knownFor: The Elements — the axiomatic, deductive method
pipeline.oneLiner: Codified geometry and the logic of proof itself — the template of rigor that defined what 'mathematics' means for over two thousand years.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches building knowledge from clear first axioms, teaching with clarity, and 'there is no royal road to geometry' — understanding is earned step by rigorous step.
pipeline.landmines: Almost nothing is known of the man — no reliable birth/death dates (only a floruit c. 300 BC), and some scholars argue 'Euclid' may name a tradition or team. The Elements compiles earlier results (Eudoxus, Theaetetus) as much as it originates them.

pipeline.name: Leo Tolstoy
pipeline.knownFor: War and Peace, Anna Karenina
pipeline.oneLiner: Widely regarded as the summit of the realist novel; unmatched at rendering whole societies and the interior life at once.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches finding meaning, moral clarity, and how to live; a guide for questions of purpose, mortality, simplifying a life, and integrity over status.
pipeline.landmines: Late-life radical moralist who renounced his own novels, wealth, and church; his ascetic, anarcho-pacifist religious phase can read as preachy. Controlling, unhappy marriage well documented.

pipeline.name: Franz Kafka
pipeline.knownFor: The Metamorphosis, The Trial
pipeline.oneLiner: Defined the modern condition so completely that his name became an adjective — 'Kafkaesque.'
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches coping with alienation, anxiety, and absurd bureaucracy, and pursuing a creative calling alongside a day job (he wrote at night while working in insurance).
pipeline.landmines: Instructed his friend Max Brod to burn all his unpublished work — publishing him (and thus 'summoning' him) arguably defies his dying wish. Oeuvre is fragmentary; his three novels are all unfinished. Life marked by anxiety, illness, and a fraught relationship with his father.

pipeline.name: Louis Pasteur
pipeline.knownFor: Germ theory, vaccination, pasteurization
pipeline.oneLiner: Proved germs cause disease and pioneered vaccines, arguably saving more human lives than any other scientist.
pipeline.mentorFit: Guides the 'chance favors the prepared mind' mindset: turning rigorous science into practical cures and products.
pipeline.landmines: His private notebooks revealed he took public credit while quietly using a rival's (Toussaint's) method for the anthrax vaccine; bitter nationalistic rivalry with Robert Koch; ethically risky human trials, notably the rabies vaccine on young Joseph Meister.

pipeline.name: Winston Churchill
pipeline.knownFor: Wartime prime minister who rallied Britain against Nazi Germany
pipeline.oneLiner: Stood alone against fascism when surrender looked rational, turning defiance and oratory into the will of a civilization at its darkest hour.
pipeline.mentorFit: Resolve and unambiguous communication in a crisis, rallying people when morale collapses, and refusing to negotiate with an existential threat.
pipeline.landmines: Committed imperialist with openly racist views; culpability debated in the 1943 Bengal famine; the WWI Gallipoli disaster; fiercely opposed Indian independence.

pipeline.name: Claude Monet
pipeline.knownFor: Founder of Impressionism; the Water Lilies
pipeline.oneLiner: Founded Impressionism — his 'Impression, Sunrise' literally named the movement — and taught the world to paint light, atmosphere, and perception instead of objects and outlines.
pipeline.mentorFit: Committing to a radical new way of seeing against ridicule; sustained series work; building a life's masterpiece (the Water Lilies) in old age despite failing eyesight.
pipeline.landmines: Little personal scandal. Main caution: 'Impressionism' as a brand can flatten a rigorous, once-radical practice into decorative wallpaper — don't mistake ubiquity for softness.

pipeline.name: Otto von Bismarck
pipeline.knownFor: Unified Germany; grandmaster of realpolitik diplomacy
pipeline.oneLiner: Forged a unified Germany through 'blood and iron,' then kept the peace with an intricate web of alliances — and invented the welfare state to outflank his rivals.
pipeline.mentorFit: Hard-nosed strategy and negotiation, engineering alliances that isolate opponents, and co-opting your opposition's own agenda to defuse it.
pipeline.landmines: Authoritarian and militaristic; deliberately provoked wars of unification; persecuted Catholics (Kulturkampf) and outlawed socialist organizing; the aggressive nationalism he stoked helped set the stage for later German catastrophe.

pipeline.name: James Watt
pipeline.knownFor: Separate-condenser steam engine that powered the Industrial Revolution
pipeline.oneLiner: His separate-condenser steam engine turned steam into the workhorse of the Industrial Revolution; the SI unit of power, the watt, carries his name.
pipeline.mentorFit: Solves 'how do I turn an incremental improvement into a world-changer' — teaches the engineer-plus-financier partnership (with Matthew Boulton) and commercializing/protecting IP.
pipeline.landmines: Aggressively used patents to block rivals' improvements (notably high-pressure steam), which many historians argue delayed engine progress by a generation.

pipeline.name: Richard Wagner
pipeline.knownFor: Revolutionized opera; the 'total artwork' (Gesamtkunstwerk)
pipeline.oneLiner: Transformed opera and Western harmony — the 'Tristan chord' cracked open the door to modernism — through monumental music dramas and the total-artwork ideal; one of music's most influential and most troubling figures.
pipeline.mentorFit: Total artistic vision and monomaniacal ambition — building an entire world, and even a custom theater (Bayreuth), around one's work. Best summoned strictly as a creative-vision archetype, NOT as a personal-life role model.
pipeline.landmines: SERIOUS. Virulent antisemitism (notably his essay 'Das Judenthum in der Musik') and his posthumous adoption as Hitler's favorite composer make him a Nazi-associated figure; his music is still effectively unperformed in Israel. Onboard with heavy guardrails and archetype-only framing — do not present him as a life mentor. His musical greatness is undisputed; his person is not a role model.

pipeline.name: John Locke
pipeline.knownFor: Empiricism, natural rights, and liberal government
pipeline.oneLiner: Supplied the ideas of natural rights, consent of the governed, tolerance, and the mind as a 'blank slate' that underwrite modern democracy and empirical thinking.
pipeline.mentorFit: Reasoning empirically from evidence rather than authority; defending individual rights, liberty, and tolerance, and questioning power without abandoning order.
pipeline.landmines: Invested in the slave-trading Royal African Company and helped draft Carolina's constitution sanctioning slavery, contradicting his liberty rhetoric; his property theory was also used to justify dispossessing Indigenous peoples.

pipeline.name: Abraham Lincoln
pipeline.knownFor: Preserved the Union and abolished slavery in the U.S. Civil War
pipeline.oneLiner: Held a fracturing nation together and ended American slavery through a rare fusion of moral clarity, political cunning, and prose that still defines leadership.
pipeline.mentorFit: Leading through existential division, holding firm on principle while cutting pragmatic deals, and moving people with plain, exact language.
pipeline.landmines: Suspended habeas corpus and expanded wartime executive power; his stated views on racial equality were limited and evolving; approved the Dakota 38 hanging, the largest mass execution in U.S. history.

pipeline.name: Leonhard Euler
pipeline.knownFor: The most prolific mathematician ever — e, i, Euler's identity, graph theory, analysis
pipeline.oneLiner: Founded or advanced nearly every branch of mathematics and most of its modern notation, producing at the highest level even after going blind.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches prolific daily output, resilience through adversity (kept working blind), and how relentless consistency builds a body of work no one has matched.
pipeline.landmines: An unusually drama-free, devout family man — great role model but a thin 'redemption arc' for storytelling; served autocratic courts (St. Petersburg, Berlin). His output is so vast it is hard to summarize crisply.

pipeline.name: Miguel de Cervantes
pipeline.knownFor: Don Quixote
pipeline.oneLiner: Author of Don Quixote — routinely voted the greatest novel ever written and widely called the first modern novel.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches resilience through failure and the balance of idealism with realism; a guide for late bloomers — he wrote his masterpiece in his late 50s after war, captivity, and prison.
pipeline.landmines: Thin, partly uncertain biography (disputed birth details). Part Two was rushed out to counter a pirated sequel. Period attitudes toward Moors and religion reflect the era.

pipeline.name: Igor Stravinsky
pipeline.knownFor: 'The Rite of Spring' and the modernist revolution
pipeline.oneLiner: The most influential composer of the 20th century — 'The Rite of Spring' literally provoked a riot at its premiere and reset the rhythmic and harmonic language of modern music.
pipeline.mentorFit: Serial reinvention across a 60-year career (Russian, neoclassical, then serial periods) and the nerve to provoke and break rules. Guidance on staying relevant by refusing to repeat yourself.
pipeline.landmines: Minor. Some contested interwar political sympathies and disputes over how much of his published prose/interviews were ghost-shaped by Robert Craft; not disqualifying.

pipeline.name: Yuri Gagarin
pipeline.knownFor: First human in space (Vostok 1, 1961)
pipeline.oneLiner: The first human being ever to leave Earth — a single orbit that broke the ultimate barrier and turned him into a symbol of hope worldwide.
pipeline.mentorFit: The courage to go first into the absolute unknown, and carrying the weight of representing something far larger than yourself with warmth and grace.
pipeline.landmines: Instrumentalized as a Soviet propaganda symbol, and his feat rode on a vast, secretive state program. Died in a 1968 jet crash whose exact cause remained officially murky for decades.

pipeline.name: Antoni Gaudí
pipeline.knownFor: Sagrada Família; Catalan Modernisme
pipeline.oneLiner: History's most recognizable and most-referenced architect (the #1 architect by fame index), who bent stone, light, and geometry into living, organic form and gave Barcelona its face.
pipeline.mentorFit: Total devotion to a singular, decades-long vision; deriving structure and design directly from nature; the discipline of working on a masterpiece you know you may never see finished.
pipeline.landmines: Deeply ascetic and idiosyncratically Catholic; his solitary vision doesn't generalize to teams or products. The Sagrada Família was nowhere near complete at his death (still under construction a century later) — a caution about unbounded scope. Died in 1926 struck by a tram.

pipeline.name: Cyrus the Great
pipeline.knownFor: Founder of the first Persian Empire and a model of tolerant rule
pipeline.oneLiner: Built the largest empire the world had yet seen and governed it by respecting local customs and faiths — statecraft as integration, not just conquest.
pipeline.mentorFit: Ruling a sprawling, diverse organization through tolerance and local autonomy, and winning the loyalty of those you absorb rather than crushing them.
pipeline.landmines: The empire was still assembled through military conquest; the benevolent, proto-'human rights' image rests partly on later idealization and his own propaganda (the Cyrus Cylinder).

pipeline.name: Hannibal Barca
pipeline.knownFor: Crossed the Alps; annihilation at Cannae
pipeline.oneLiner: The supreme tactician whose double-envelopment at Cannae remains the textbook model of the perfect battle, studied by every war college since.
pipeline.mentorFit: Out-thinking a stronger opponent, tactical creativity, doing the logistically impossible, and winning asymmetric fights against superior resources.
pipeline.landmines: Ravaged the Italian countryside for 15 years with heavy civilian and military toll (tens of thousands died in a single day at Cannae). Fewer massacre allegations than most on this list, but ultimately lost the war and Carthage was later destroyed.

pipeline.name: Michael Faraday
pipeline.knownFor: Electromagnetic induction, electrochemistry
pipeline.oneLiner: The self-taught bookbinder who discovered induction and gave the world electric power.
pipeline.mentorFit: Guides rising from poverty through relentless self-education and peerless hands-on experimentation and curiosity.
pipeline.landmines: Very few, and a man of deep integrity (he refused to develop chemical weapons for the Crimean War). Lacked mathematical training, so Maxwell later had to formalize his physical intuitions; suffered memory loss late in life.

pipeline.name: George Washington
pipeline.knownFor: Led American independence and defined the U.S. presidency
pipeline.oneLiner: Won a revolution and then voluntarily surrendered power — twice — writing the template for democratic leadership that restrains itself.
pipeline.mentorFit: Leading on character over charisma, and having the discipline to relinquish power and institutionalize succession instead of clinging on.
pipeline.landmines: Enslaved more than 300 people across his lifetime; ordered brutal scorched-earth campaigns against the Iroquois (Haudenosaunee) nations.

pipeline.name: Neil Armstrong
pipeline.knownFor: First human to walk on the Moon (Apollo 11, 1969)
pipeline.oneLiner: Took humanity's first step onto another world — arguably the single most significant act of exploration in history — and did it with legendary calm.
pipeline.mentorFit: Precision and composure under literal life-or-death pressure; profound humility in the face of historic achievement and a lifetime of relentless fame you never sought.
pipeline.landmines: None of real consequence; an intensely private man who deliberately declined to trade on or commercialize his fame.

pipeline.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
pipeline.knownFor: New Deal architect and WWII leader; four-term U.S. president
pipeline.oneLiner: Steered a nation through the Great Depression and a world war, rebuilding the modern state and forging a global alliance while projecting unshakeable calm.
pipeline.mentorFit: Leading through back-to-back catastrophes with visible optimism, building broad coalitions, and reinventing institutions fast enough to meet the crisis.
pipeline.landmines: Ordered the internment of ~120,000 Japanese-Americans; attempted to pack the Supreme Court; turned away Jewish refugees fleeing the Holocaust; concentrated unprecedented executive power.

pipeline.name: Frederick the Great
pipeline.knownFor: Prussian king, master of the outnumbered battle
pipeline.oneLiner: Held off a coalition of great powers through the Seven Years' War, perfecting the oblique order at Leuthen and Rossbach and directly inspiring Napoleon.
pipeline.mentorFit: Resilience against long odds, fighting and winning while outnumbered, discipline and drill, and enduring adversity without breaking (the philosopher-king commander).
pipeline.landmines: Launched wars of aggression — the unprovoked seizure of Silesia triggered decades of continental war costing hundreds of thousands of lives; harsh military discipline; authored antisemitic policies and writings; autocratic ruler.

pipeline.name: Niels Bohr
pipeline.knownFor: Quantum model of the atom, Copenhagen interpretation
pipeline.oneLiner: Founded the quantum picture of the atom and mentored the generation that built modern physics.
pipeline.mentorFit: Guides building a world-leading institute and collaborative culture, and reasoning clearly through paradox and complementarity.
pipeline.landmines: His complementarity / Copenhagen interpretation remains philosophically contested; the ambiguous 1941 wartime meeting with Heisenberg; he advised the Manhattan Project; his dense, opaque speaking and writing style frustrated even admirers.

pipeline.name: Bernhard Riemann
pipeline.knownFor: Riemannian geometry, complex analysis, the Riemann Hypothesis
pipeline.oneLiner: Bent geometry into the curved-space mathematics that Einstein would need, and posed the deepest unsolved problem in all of mathematics.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches thinking in bold abstractions decades ahead of your era, and following one profound idea deeper than anyone else dares to go.
pipeline.landmines: Died at 39 (tuberculosis) with a small but seismic output; shy, sickly, financially strained. His work is highly technical, limiting mass-audience mentor content; the Riemann Hypothesis is still open (no tidy 'solved it' arc).

pipeline.name: Alexander Graham Bell
pipeline.knownFor: The telephone
pipeline.oneLiner: Patented the telephone and founded the company that became AT&T, launching the global telecommunications era from work at the intersection of sound, speech, and machinery.
pipeline.mentorFit: Solves 'how do I turn a lab breakthrough into world-spanning infrastructure and a company' — teaches invention driven by a mission (his was teaching the deaf) that becomes industry.
pipeline.landmines: Bitter, still-debated priority disputes (Elisha Gray, Antonio Meucci). Later a prominent advocate of eugenics and of oralism that suppressed sign language — deeply harmful to the Deaf community.

pipeline.name: Coco Chanel
pipeline.knownFor: The house of Chanel and modern luxury branding
pipeline.oneLiner: Freed women from the corset and built an enduring luxury house on a singular personal brand — arguably the most influential figure in the business of fashion.
pipeline.mentorFit: Build a magnetic personal brand, strip away everything unnecessary, and reinvent yourself again and again. For designers, founders, and anyone building a taste-driven brand.
pipeline.landmines: Severe: a Nazi collaborator during WWII — an Abwehr agent (Operation Modellhut) in a relationship with a German intelligence officer — who tried to use Aryanization laws to seize her perfume business from its Jewish owners, the Wertheimers. Documented antisemitism. A high-risk mentor pick.

pipeline.name: Charles Dickens
pipeline.knownFor: Great Expectations, A Tale of Two Cities, Oliver Twist
pipeline.oneLiner: The greatest Victorian novelist; created an unmatched gallery of characters and fused mass popularity with lasting art.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches prolific output and work ethic, reinvention from childhood poverty, and building a mass audience; a guide for storytelling wielded for social change and for the business of serialized, audience-first creative work.
pipeline.landmines: Cruelly separated from his wife Catherine and tried to publicly discredit her; long-concealed affair with young actress Ellen Ternan. Prone to sentimentality and caricature; the character Fagin is widely criticized as an antisemitic stereotype.

pipeline.name: Ashoka
pipeline.knownFor: Mauryan emperor who renounced war for ethical governance
pipeline.oneLiner: After a war so bloody it broke him, he rebuilt his rule around ethics, public welfare, and religious tolerance — imperial power redirected by conscience.
pipeline.mentorFit: Transformation after a moral reckoning, and governing by declared values, welfare, and restraint rather than by force.
pipeline.landmines: His early reign was violent and reportedly ruthless ('Ashoka the Fierce'); the Kalinga war he waged killed and displaced hundreds of thousands before his conversion.

pipeline.name: Ibn Battuta
pipeline.knownFor: 24 years and ~117,000 km across the medieval Islamic world and beyond
pipeline.oneLiner: Traveled farther than any explorer of the pre-modern era — roughly three times Marco Polo's distance — leaving in the Rihla an unrivaled eyewitness map of the 14th-century world.
pipeline.mentorFit: Adapting to any culture on Earth, leveraging your skills and credentials to fund a life of exploration, and treating lifelong curiosity as a genuine vocation.
pipeline.landmines: A serial slave owner and master of concubines, even by the norms of his era; scholars flag exaggeration and several likely-fabricated legs of the journey, since the Rihla was reconstructed from memory years later and polished by a court scribe.

pipeline.name: Guru Nanak
pipeline.knownFor: Founder of Sikhism
pipeline.oneLiner: Founder of Sikhism, the world's fifth-largest organized religion, preaching one God, human equality and honest living centuries ahead of his era.
pipeline.mentorFit: Radical equality across caste, creed and gender; balancing devotion with worldly duty; honest work; and selfless service to others (seva).
pipeline.landmines: Religious-figure — onboarding requires extra sensitivity; Sikhs venerate the ten Gurus and traditionally avoid depicting them, so a first-person persona may offend. Well-dated (1469–1539). Lower global notability signals reflect Sikhism's geographic concentration, not lesser stature.

pipeline.name: Roald Amundsen
pipeline.knownFor: First to the South Pole; first to both poles and through the Northwest Passage
pipeline.oneLiner: The greatest polar explorer — won the race to the South Pole through obsessive preparation and by humbly learning Inuit survival techniques while rivals died improvising.
pipeline.mentorFit: Achieving audacious goals through relentless preparation rather than heroics; the humility to adopt proven methods from others; disciplined risk management and single-minded focus.
pipeline.landmines: Criticized for secrecy in quietly switching his announced Arctic expedition into a South Pole race against Scott, whose party perished on the return. Relied on the planned slaughter of his own sled dogs for food. Minor beside his peers; he died in 1928 flying a rescue mission for a rival.

pipeline.name: Walt Disney
pipeline.knownFor: The animation studio, theme park, and media franchise
pipeline.oneLiner: Turned a mouse cartoon into the world's most valuable entertainment franchise system — animation, theme parks, licensing, and brand — inventing the modern media empire.
pipeline.mentorFit: Marry a creative vision to commercial systems and build a brand and universe, not just a product. For creative founders and product, brand, and studio leaders.
pipeline.landmines: Fought the 1941 animators' strike bitterly, named names as an FBI/HUAC informant during the Red Scare, ran an autocratic operation, and early works carry racial stereotypes (e.g., 'Song of the South'). Cross-domain: also fits Arts & Entertainment.

pipeline.name: Katsushika Hokusai
pipeline.knownFor: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
pipeline.oneLiner: Japan's greatest artist, whose 'Great Wave' is among the most reproduced images ever made and whose prints ignited the Japonisme that reshaped Van Gogh, Monet, and Degas — the essential non-Western master.
pipeline.mentorFit: Lifelong, humble pursuit of improvement (he said real progress would only come at 100); reinvention — he changed his name 30+ times — and sheer productivity across 30,000+ works.
pipeline.landmines: Few personal landmines beyond a chaotic, impoverished life and constant moves. Main caution is Western over-reduction of a vast, restless body of work to a single wave — resist flattening him to one image.

pipeline.name: Zheng He
pipeline.knownFor: Commanded Ming China's seven treasure-fleet voyages to Africa
pipeline.oneLiner: Admiral of the largest wooden ships and fleets the world had ever seen, projecting Ming power across the Indian Ocean to Arabia and East Africa decades before Columbus set sail.
pipeline.mentorFit: Rising from prisoner of war to grand admiral of the age; commanding vast logistics at scale; projecting influence through diplomacy and sheer presence rather than conquest.
pipeline.landmines: The voyages were state power-projection, and Zheng He did use force — crushing a warlord at Palembang and intervening militarily in Ceylon. He was a eunuch, castrated and conscripted as a boy after his father was killed in the Ming conquest of Yunnan.

pipeline.name: James Cook
pipeline.knownFor: Three Pacific voyages mapping New Zealand, eastern Australia, and Hawaii
pipeline.oneLiner: The greatest scientific navigator — charted more of the Earth's surface than anyone before him and beat scurvy by obsessively guarding his crew's health.
pipeline.mentorFit: Rising from farm laborer to captain purely on merit; disciplined, evidence-based preparation; treating your team's health and wellbeing as a core leadership duty, not an afterthought.
pipeline.landmines: His charts opened the Pacific to colonization, disease, and dispossession; he claimed Australia under the legal fiction of terra nullius and was killed in a violent confrontation at Kealakekua Bay, Hawaii. His legacy is deeply contested among Indigenous Pacific and Australian peoples.

pipeline.name: Aretha Franklin
pipeline.knownFor: The Queen of Soul
pipeline.oneLiner: The definitive voice of soul and one of the greatest singers ever recorded; she turned gospel fervor and personal struggle into anthems of dignity and demand, above all 'Respect'.
pipeline.mentorFit: Authentic voice and self-respect — a woman who claimed her power in a male-dominated industry and transmuted personal pain into strength. Guidance on demanding your worth and finding an unmistakable voice; strong brand/voice archetype.
pipeline.landmines: Modern figure: recordings, image, and likeness are controlled by her estate and record labels, so rights clearance is needed for onboarding. Personal life was private and at times difficult — keep the persona respectful and non-invasive.

pipeline.name: Sun Tzu
pipeline.knownFor: Author of The Art of War
pipeline.oneLiner: The foundational strategist whose 2,500-year-old treatise still defines how the world thinks about strategy, deception, positioning, and winning without fighting.
pipeline.mentorFit: Strategy itself: knowing self and opponent, winning before the battle, deception and positioning, and building durable competitive advantage.
pipeline.landmines: A semi-legendary figure whose historical existence and sole authorship of the text are debated by scholars. The famous legend of executing the king's concubines to prove discipline, if true, is brutal; otherwise minimal atrocity record because minimal verified biography.

pipeline.name: John Maynard Keynes
pipeline.knownFor: Keynesian macroeconomics; The General Theory
pipeline.oneLiner: Reinvented macroeconomics and defined how modern governments fight recessions.
pipeline.mentorFit: Navigate uncertainty, demand, and downturns; when to spend vs. save, why 'animal spirits' move markets, and how to act amid the unknowable.
pipeline.landmines: Held eugenics-era views (led the Eugenics Society) and made antisemitic remarks in private writings. His economics is politically contested (deficit-spending debates); critics on the right reject the whole framework.

pipeline.name: Khalid ibn al-Walid
pipeline.knownFor: The undefeated 'Sword of Allah'
pipeline.oneLiner: Never lost a battle across roughly 100 engagements, shattering both the Byzantine and Sasanian armies to launch the early Islamic conquests.
pipeline.mentorFit: Undefeated execution, mobility and surprise, seizing the initiative, and repeatedly winning against numerically superior forces.
pipeline.landmines: Brutal in the Ridda Wars and the conquests; the killing of Malik ibn Nuwayra and immediate marriage to his widow remains a lasting controversy in Islamic historiography; executions of prisoners in some campaigns; wars of religious conquest.

pipeline.name: Henry Ford
pipeline.knownFor: Moving assembly line and mass production
pipeline.oneLiner: The moving assembly line and the $5 workday made the automobile a mass product and rewrote how the world manufactures everything — effectively the birth of modern industry.
