pipeline.mentorFit: Solves 'how do I scale production and slash unit cost' — the operations/manufacturing-department archetype: systems thinking, throughput, and paying workers enough to buy the product.
pipeline.landmines: Virulent antisemite — funded and published 'The International Jew'; praised by Hitler and accepted a Nazi medal (1938). A monumental industrial legacy paired with genuinely repugnant bigotry; unsuitable as a moral role model and must be framed carefully.

pipeline.name: James Clerk Maxwell
pipeline.knownFor: Electromagnetism, Maxwell's equations
pipeline.oneLiner: Unified electricity, magnetism, and light into four equations: physics' second great unification after Newton.
pipeline.mentorFit: Guides synthesizing scattered phenomena into elegant predictive theory, and quiet mastery over self-promotion.
pipeline.landmines: Remarkably few; devout and modest by all accounts. Died at just 48 of abdominal cancer, cutting his work short, and remains badly underappreciated by the public relative to his colossal influence on modern physics.

pipeline.name: Warren Buffett
pipeline.knownFor: Greatest value investor; Berkshire Hathaway
pipeline.oneLiner: Compounded a failing textile mill into a trillion-dollar empire and became the definitive long-term investor.
pipeline.mentorFit: Long-term value investing, patience, circle of competence, compounding, and temperament over raw intelligence.
pipeline.landmines: Living person (age 95) — verify current status before publishing; stepped down as Berkshire CEO in Jan 2026 (Greg Abel succeeded him) but remains chairman. Never present his views as personalized investment advice. Folksy image masks hard-nosed dealmaking; longtime partner Charlie Munger is already onboarded, so position Buffett as the complementary pairing.

pipeline.name: David Hilbert
pipeline.knownFor: The 23 problems, formalism, Hilbert spaces
pipeline.oneLiner: Set the agenda for twentieth-century mathematics with his 23 problems and championed rigorous formal foundations for the whole field.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches setting bold, clarifying goals that mobilize a generation ('we must know — we will know'), building a school, and optimism that hard problems are solvable.
pipeline.landmines: His formalist program — a complete, consistent, provable foundation for mathematics — was famously demolished by Gödel's incompleteness theorems. Work is technical for lay audiences; Göttingen's golden age was destroyed by Nazi purges he could not stop.

pipeline.name: Jane Austen
pipeline.knownFor: Pride and Prejudice
pipeline.oneLiner: Perfected the novel of manners and pioneered free indirect style; one of the most beloved and endlessly re-read authors in English.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches social intelligence, reading people, and irony as a tool; a guide for clear-eyed realism about money, class, and relationships beneath polite surfaces.
pipeline.landmines: Lower raw notability signals than the top tier, but a fixture of every serious all-time canon on craft alone. Narrow social/geographic range (English landed gentry) and near-silence on the slavery/colonial economy underwriting that world draws live modern critique. Sparse personal record — her sister burned most of her letters.

pipeline.name: Louis Armstrong
pipeline.knownFor: Jazz's first great soloist; foundation of modern popular music
pipeline.oneLiner: The most pivotal figure in the birth of jazz and, through it, all modern popular music — his trumpet and voice invented the vocabulary of the improvising soloist and swing.
pipeline.mentorFit: Rising from deep poverty to reinvent an entire art form through virtuosity, charisma, and sheer joy. Guidance on turning hardship into generosity and making mastery look like delight.
pipeline.landmines: Was criticized during the civil-rights era as too accommodating (the 'Uncle Tom' charge) before his outspoken 1957 Little Rock stand rebutted it — context worth handling with nuance rather than omitting.

pipeline.name: David Ricardo
pipeline.knownFor: Comparative advantage
pipeline.oneLiner: Formalized comparative advantage — still the bedrock argument for trade and specialization.
pipeline.mentorFit: Focus your effort where your relative edge is greatest; specialize and trade rather than trying to do everything yourself.
pipeline.landmines: Made his fortune partly via government-bond speculation (famously around Waterloo). The labor theory of value and abstract 'Ricardian' assumptions are heavily contested as unrealistic; strongest as a single-idea guide.

pipeline.name: Srinivasa Ramanujan
pipeline.knownFor: Self-taught genius; ~3,900 results in number theory and analysis
pipeline.oneLiner: A poor, largely self-taught clerk who produced thousands of astonishing formulas from raw intuition — results mathematicians are still unpacking a century later.
pipeline.mentorFit: The ultimate outsider-genius story: teaches trusting raw intuition, self-teaching from almost nothing, and finding the mentor (Hardy) who unlocks a hidden gift against every odds.
pipeline.landmines: Died at 32; attributed formulas to a family goddess (the myth can overshadow the mathematics); some notebook claims were informal or unproven. Marginal #10 pick: Henri Poincaré (HPI 81.5, founder of topology and chaos) and Georg Cantor (HPI 78.4, set theory of infinity) rank near-equal and are the closest omissions — Ramanujan is placed here partly for his exceptional life-mentor value. Emmy Noether (abstract algebra) is the strongest woman just outside the ten.

pipeline.name: Kurt Gödel
pipeline.knownFor: The incompleteness theorems
pipeline.oneLiner: Proved that any sufficiently rich formal system harbors true statements it can never prove — the deepest and most unsettling result in modern logic.
pipeline.mentorFit: Teaches the limits of formal knowledge, rigorous skepticism about what can be proven, and the courage to overturn a whole field's assumptions with one airtight argument.
pipeline.landmines: Severe paranoia and depression; died of self-starvation fearing poisoning — a sensitive, tragic figure, not a wholesome 'life coach.' His theorems are abstract and are endlessly mangled into pseudo-profound misquotes. Adjacent logic titans Alan Turing and Alonzo Church are ceded to the Computing domain.

pipeline.name: Jamsetji Tata
pipeline.knownFor: Founder of the Tata Group and modern Indian industry
pipeline.oneLiner: Founded Indian heavy industry — steel, hydroelectric power, and world-class hospitality — decades ahead of independence, proving industrial ambition and ethics could coexist.
pipeline.mentorFit: Build for the long term and for the nation, treat workers well ahead of your era, and let ethics compound into trust. For founders who want to build institutions that outlive them.
pipeline.landmines: Comparatively clean legacy, but built inside the British colonial economy and founded a dynastic conglomerate whose later scale raises concentration questions. Wealth was inherited-and-expanded, not purely self-made.

pipeline.name: Friedrich Hayek
pipeline.knownFor: Austrian economics; The Road to Serfdom
pipeline.oneLiner: Nobel laureate who defended markets, prices, and liberty against central planning.
pipeline.mentorFit: Respect decentralized knowledge and emergent order; humility about how little any planner (or leader) can centrally know or control.
pipeline.landmines: Icon of the political right; his visit to and comments on Pinochet's Chile are a recurring attack line. A polarizing figure in ideological debates — pair with Keynes for balance.

pipeline.name: Horatio Nelson
pipeline.knownFor: Britain's greatest admiral, victor of Trafalgar
pipeline.oneLiner: Revolutionized naval tactics with aggressive, decisive action — destroying enemy fleets at the Nile and Trafalgar — to secure a century of British sea power (the list's sole naval master).
pipeline.mentorFit: Bold, decisive action, calculated risk, trusting empowered subordinates (his 'band of brothers'), and morale-driven leadership that wins against the odds.
pipeline.landmines: Actively defended the slave trade and attacked abolitionists in writing; complicit in the brutal 1799 reprisals against Neapolitan republican rebels (reneged surrender terms; the execution of Caracciolo); a notorious public affair with Emma Hamilton.

pipeline.name: Frank Lloyd Wright
pipeline.knownFor: Fallingwater; organic architecture
pipeline.oneLiner: The defining architect of the American century — 1,000+ designs across 70 years, the Guggenheim and Fallingwater among them, and a whole philosophy (organic architecture) for how buildings should meet the land.
pipeline.mentorFit: Building a coherent design philosophy and personal brand; reinventing a career repeatedly after scandal and financial ruin; harmonizing what you make with its environment.
pipeline.landmines: Lowest fame index of the ten (HPI 77.46) — architecture indexes far below painting on Wikipedia-based metrics, and Le Corbusier (86.85) and Cézanne (85.32) both outscore him; he's included for architecture coverage and product fit, not raw notability. Serial self-mythologizer with a vast ego; chronic debt; abandoned his family in a public scandal; buildings famous for leaking roofs and overruns. The 1914 Taliesin murders were a tragedy inflicted on him — handle with care.

pipeline.name: Milton Friedman
pipeline.knownFor: Monetarism and free-market economics
pipeline.oneLiner: Led the free-market counter-revolution and reshaped monetary policy across the world.
pipeline.mentorFit: Reason from free-market first principles; the case for personal and economic freedom, and healthy skepticism toward central intervention.
pipeline.landmines: Highly polarizing. The 'Chicago Boys' / Pinochet-Chile association is a standard attack line; critics blame his ideology for inequality and deregulation. Balance with the opposing (Keynes/Hayek) framings.

pipeline.name: Estée Lauder
pipeline.knownFor: Self-made cosmetics empire built on sampling and touch
pipeline.oneLiner: Started at a kitchen table and built a global cosmetics empire on face-to-face selling and the free sample, becoming one of history's great self-made businesswomen.
pipeline.mentorFit: Sell person-to-person, let people try before they buy, and out-hustle bigger, better-funded rivals. For founders bootstrapping a consumer brand and for marketing and sales teams.
pipeline.landmines: Largely clean; known for a ferociously aggressive competitive streak (notably against Revlon's Charles Revson) and for polishing over her humble immigrant origins with a grander, partly invented backstory.

pipeline.name: Subutai
pipeline.knownFor: Mongol grand strategist of the Eurasian conquests
pipeline.oneLiner: Directed campaigns across the widest theater any general has ever commanded — winning 60+ battles and coordinating multi-army operations from China to Hungary centuries ahead of his era — yet remains under-recognized versus his notability rank.
pipeline.mentorFit: Operational planning, intelligence and reconnaissance, orchestrating complex multi-front campaigns — the executor who turns grand vision into reality (a pure operations/execution archetype).
pipeline.landmines: A principal architect of the Mongol conquests and their massacres — Khwarazmia, northern China, and the annihilating invasions of Rus and Hungary — sharing fully in the Mongol atrocity record of city-wide slaughter.

pipeline.name: Tim Berners-Lee
pipeline.knownFor: Inventor of the World Wide Web
pipeline.oneLiner: Invented the Web — HTTP, HTML, and the URL — in 1989 and, crucially, gave it away royalty-free, creating the open platform the modern world runs on.
pipeline.mentorFit: Solves 'how do I build something universal and open rather than a walled garden' — teaches designing standards, building for everyone, and choosing long-term public good over personal fortune.
pipeline.landmines: Few and mild — later ventures (the Solid project, and a 2021 NFT auction of the Web's original source code) drew modest criticism; a technologist more than a manager. Living figure, so his legacy is still unfolding.

pipeline.name: Mayer Amschel Rothschild
pipeline.knownFor: Founder of the Rothschild banking dynasty
pipeline.oneLiner: Built the first truly international banking house and the template for modern cross-border finance.
pipeline.mentorFit: Build durable financial networks and multi-generational capital; the power of trust, information advantage, and family/institutional coordination.
pipeline.landmines: MAJOR: the Rothschild name is the center of persistent antisemitic conspiracy theories about banking and world control. Must be handled factually and carefully; high risk of attracting or appearing to endorse conspiracy narratives. Better as a finance archetype than a personal life-mentor.

pipeline.name: J.P. Morgan
pipeline.knownFor: The most powerful financier in American history
pipeline.oneLiner: Twice acted as a one-man central bank before the Fed existed, and assembled U.S. Steel and General Electric — the closest any private citizen has come to owning the American economy.
pipeline.mentorFit: Deploy capital with conviction, structure and close hard deals, and impose order on chaos. For finance leaders, dealmakers, and founders raising or consolidating — a natural finance-department archetype.
pipeline.landmines: Archetypal robber baron — engineered monopolies (Northern Securities), wielded unaccountable 'money trust' power (Pujo hearings), and profited from the bailouts he arranged. A symbol of Gilded Age wealth concentration.

pipeline.name: Andrew Carnegie
pipeline.knownFor: Steel empire and modern large-scale philanthropy
pipeline.oneLiner: Rose from a bobbin boy to the richest man in the world through ruthless vertical integration, then gave nearly all of it away and defined how the wealthy are expected to give.
pipeline.mentorFit: Control your costs and your supply chain to win, then decide what your wealth is actually for. For operators obsessed with margin and anyone wrestling with purpose after success.
pipeline.landmines: The 1892 Homestead Strike: Pinkertons and state militia broke his steelworkers, several killed and wages slashed, while he cultivated a philanthropic image from abroad. Brutal hours and conditions built the fortune.

pipeline.name: Ernest Shackleton
pipeline.knownFor: The Endurance expedition — survival after his ship was crushed in Antarctic ice
pipeline.oneLiner: Failed his goal of crossing Antarctica but pulled off the greatest survival-leadership feat in history — bringing all 28 men home alive across ice, ocean, and an 800-mile open-boat voyage.
pipeline.mentorFit: Leading through total catastrophe: keeping a team alive and hopeful when the plan collapses, adapting relentlessly, and putting your people's survival above the mission itself. The definitive expedition-leadership mentor for courage and resilience.
pipeline.landmines: Never actually achieved his stated expedition objectives and was a chronically poor businessman, dogged by debt and failed ventures. The archetypal 'heroic failure' whose greatness lives in the rescue, not the goal.

pipeline.name: Duke Ellington
pipeline.knownFor: America's greatest jazz composer and bandleader
pipeline.oneLiner: Elevated jazz into a sophisticated concert art form — composing 1,000+ works and leading his orchestra for nearly 50 years, writing specifically to the unique voice of each player.
pipeline.mentorFit: Leading a creative team for decades: Ellington composed FOR his musicians' individual strengths. The archetype of the bandleader-manager who draws a lifetime of great work out of a group — a natural fit for team/engineering leadership.
pipeline.landmines: None significant.

pipeline.name: Ray Kroc
pipeline.knownFor: Franchised McDonald's into the global fast-food system
pipeline.oneLiner: Took a single hamburger stand and, through relentless standardization and franchising, built the operating system for global fast food and the modern franchise itself.
pipeline.mentorFit: Standardize quality obsessively, franchise for scale, and stay hungry at any age. For operators scaling a repeatable unit and anyone starting over late in life.
pipeline.landmines: Squeezed out the McDonald brothers who created the restaurant — reneging on a handshake royalty deal and opening a rival store to pressure them — and ran a hard system on franchisees.

pipeline.name: Benjamin Graham
pipeline.knownFor: Father of value investing; The Intelligent Investor
pipeline.oneLiner: Invented security analysis and value investing — and personally taught Warren Buffett.
pipeline.mentorFit: Value-investing discipline: margin of safety, treating 'Mr. Market' as a servant not a guide, and separating investing from speculation.
pipeline.landmines: Fame is fairly niche outside investing. Some specific techniques (deep-value 'net-nets') are dated; died in 1976, so he has no view on modern markets. Positioned close to Buffett, so differentiate the mentor angle.

pipeline.name: Cornelius Vanderbilt
pipeline.knownFor: Shipping and railroad empire; the original American tycoon
pipeline.oneLiner: Built one of the largest fortunes in human history from nothing, out-competing every rival on water and then rail, and set the template for the self-made industrial titan.
pipeline.mentorFit: Compete without flinching, spot the next transport or technology shift early, and reinvest relentlessly. For the founder who needs nerve, timing, and killer instinct.
pipeline.landmines: Ruthless monopolist and stock manipulator (the Erie War), crushed competitors, paid workers poorly, and gave away comparatively little of an enormous fortune. The 'robber baron' label effectively starts with him.

pipeline.name: Andy Grove
pipeline.knownFor: The operator who scaled Intel and wrote the management playbook
pipeline.oneLiner: Escaped the Holocaust and Soviet Hungary, ran Intel through the microprocessor revolution, and wrote the books ('High Output Management,' 'Only the Paranoid Survive') that still define how operators lead.
pipeline.mentorFit: Run a high-output team, confront reality early ('only the paranoid survive'), and navigate strategic inflection points before they sink you. The definitive mentor for managers and operators — a standout operations archetype.
pipeline.landmines: An abrasive, confrontational management culture ('constructive confrontation') that some found brutal; presided over Intel's initially defensive, tone-deaf handling of the 1994 Pentium FDIV recall.

pipeline.name: John Bogle
pipeline.knownFor: Inventor of the index fund; founder of Vanguard
pipeline.oneLiner: Democratized investing by inventing the low-cost index fund, saving ordinary investors trillions in fees.
pipeline.mentorFit: Keep costs low, buy the whole market, ignore the noise, and let compounding work; a fiduciary, don't-try-to-be-clever mindset for everyday wealth.
pipeline.landmines: Relatively uncontroversial but niche in fame. Main debate is the critique that mass passive indexing distorts markets and concentrates corporate ownership. Died 2019.

pipeline.name: Wright brothers
pipeline.knownFor: First powered, controlled, heavier-than-air flight (1903)
pipeline.oneLiner: Two self-funded bicycle mechanics solved controlled powered flight in 1903 — cracking three-axis control that the era's best-funded rivals could not — and founded aviation.
pipeline.mentorFit: Solves 'how does a scrappy, underfunded team beat richer competitors' — teaches disciplined experimentation (they built their own wind tunnel) and attacking the hard sub-problem (control, not just thrust) everyone else ignored.
pipeline.landmines: Years of aggressive patent litigation (the 'patent wars', especially vs. Glenn Curtiss) are widely argued to have stunted early US aviation. HPI unavailable on Pantheon (they are indexed individually, not as a pair).

pipeline.name: The Beatles
pipeline.knownFor: The most influential band in history
pipeline.oneLiner: The most commercially successful and influential act of the rock era; in barely a decade they reinvented songwriting, the recording studio, and global youth culture.
pipeline.mentorFit: The archetype of a legendary creative team — the Lennon–McCartney partnership, constant reinvention, and how four people compounded into something none could achieve alone. Uniquely strong as a collaboration / department-team archetype.
pipeline.landmines: This is a GROUP, not one person — the index schema is person-shaped. For a single-human life-mentor guide, use John Lennon (d. 1980, HPI 83.61) or Paul McCartney (living, HPI 79.53); the band is the stronger team-archetype. Two members are living (McCartney, Starr) plus estates, so name/likeness and music rights (Apple Corps, Sony Music Publishing) require clearance. Flag for onboarding.
